A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAR framework. Their complete text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the revised title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original VAR benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and capability analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains original VAR benchmark results, component ablations, and capability analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same grounded reasoning trajectory, four-component reward, constrained depth-first search with backtracking, and SFT followed by GRPO. The hierarchical-search terminology does not introduce a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training still uses VGR-158K-derived data and SSUI in VAR-RL-32K. The ten main benchmarks and additional Table 2 tasks are retained. Segmentation and point prompts are proposed only as future extensions.

E2.justification: Qwen2.5-VL-72B disappears from Table 1 but remains in Figure 1’s comparison on the same ten benchmarks and in Table 2. Thus its evaluated comparator coverage remains documented. The other comparison methods are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported training configuration, 32,800-sample RL dataset, benchmark procedures, accuracy measures, and default comparator settings remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains all eight settings testing initialization, traceability rewards, backtracking, and text-only RL. The capability-correlation analysis and illustrated reasoning case are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report empirical point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The theoretical probability bound is not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 removes the Qwen2.5-VL-72B numerical row, including its 64.2 average, and the VAR-minus-72B differences; its benchmark curve remains in Figure 1. All retained table scores are unchanged. Section 3.4 changes the claimed near-match from the 72B model to the 32B model despite unchanged HalB scores.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 changes its guarantee from at least 1−4δ in v1 Appendix A.1 to at least 1−2δ in v2 Appendix A. The revised proof removes the approximate justification for the looser bound and consistently concludes 1−2δ, which v1 already derived. The assumptions, exploration budget, and complexity bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit claim to be the first framework unifying grounded evidence, learnable search with backtracking, and self-verification rewards. Its conclusion also removes v1’s open-source qualification from the state-of-the-art claim. The underlying contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: A new Limitations section explains that bounding boxes inadequately represent irregular shapes and pixel-level details, suggesting segmentation masks or point prompts as future remedies. The existing mechanism explanations and ablation interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same base model, LLaMA-Factory implementation, eight A100 GPUs, AdamW settings, batch size, learning-rate schedule, and data filtering. Appendix information about conditioning and validation is retained, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the dedicated Related Works section rather than relocating it, substantially reducing discussion of reward design, curriculum RL, AI feedback, and image-tool reasoning. References including Visionary-R1, LMM-R1, RLAIF-V, and Chain-of-Focus disappear. Two overview citations are added, alongside the stronger first-framework positioning.

P1.justification: The title, author line, abstract, conclusion, and appendix prose are edited. Related Works is removed, Limitations is added, and appendices A.1–A.3 become A–C. Most method and experimental prose remains unchanged, making the editorial reorganization limited.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column layout to two columns, with substantially different float placement and equation formatting. The same three figures are retained and resized or relocated; Tables 2–3 retain their content, while Table 1 loses two rows.

improvement.justification: The consistent Lemma 1 bound and concrete bounding-box limitation improve clarity. However, v2 removes substantial related-work context while strengthening novelty claims and reduces the main numerical comparison. It also introduces a misleading HalB near-match claim: VAR’s 55.5 is compared with the 32B model’s 48.1 instead of the 72B model’s 55.6. These changes modestly weaken evidential precision and positioning overall.
